key_points: A self-assessment test to evaluate the rotational mobility of the upper body (thoracic spine/rib cage) while maintaining lower body stability.

Lying in a prone position can cause the spine, particularly the upper thoracic spine, to extend or flatten. This extended spinal position compromises the scapula's ability to maintain congruence (flush contact) with the naturally rounded, convex thoracic ribcage, thereby hindering effective scapular gliding and rotation, which is crucial for optimal lower trapezius function.

This exercise aims to improve rib cage expansion and opening on the side of the winged shoulder blade by using a side plank position with the top arm extended overhead, focusing on relaxed breathing to facilitate rib cage mobility.
